title: SGD on a bowl-shaped loss
description: A blue bowl-shaped loss surface with contour lines; a dark dot marks the lowest point at its center. A red ball takes one stochastic gradient descent step per tick and leaves an orange trail. A purple arrow starting at the ball's edge shows the noisy step it is about to take. The steep (across) direction runs left-right on screen. Drag the ball left-right, or the green knob on the rail along the bowl's left rim front-back, to pick a new start. Readouts show loss, gradient size, steps and status.
assumptions: Illustration: a simple formula-defined bowl with simulated noise, not a model trained on real data.

Loss = steepness × across² + along² (across is left-right on screen). The surface is drawn at height 0.2 × loss; it gets narrower across as steepness rises (half-width 3/√steepness), so contours stay true loss levels.

Each step subtracts learning rate × (true gradient + noise), the noise drawn from a bell curve with the chosen spread in each direction. A single step can raise the loss; it falls only on average. Above 1 ÷ steepness the across swings grow.
The purple arrow is the next step (noise included), drawn from the ball's edge at 4 times its true length (one fixed scale), flat in the across-along plane. It is hidden when the run has stopped.

A run stops after 200 steps, with noise 0 when the gradient size falls below 0.01 (converged), or as diverged once the ball is 3 surface half-widths out across or past the along edge. Off the surface the ball and trail are drawn at the rim; readouts stay exact.
The trail marks every step (up to 201 points), not every 2nd as planned, because sampling every 2nd step would hide the zig-zag.

Dragging the ball (across) or the green knob on the left rim rail (along) sets a new start and clears the trail and step count; it also draws fresh noise. Random numbers come from a fixed seed, so Reset repeats the same run.
